best_architecture: Use discord.py (v2.x) as the gateway client running on a single shared asyncio event loop, with the LLM/agent orchestrator integrated as cooperative async tasks rather than blocking calls. The recommended pattern is a hybrid 'bot + webhook' design: a persistent Bot (WebSocket gateway) for interactive, bidirectional flows (slash commands, mentions, replies, threads), and outbound Webhooks for one-way agent notifications that do not need a gateway connection. Critical design decisions, in order of importance: (1) Never block the event loop - the agent/LLM call MUST be awaitable; if the orchestrator exposes only synchronous APIs, wrap them with loop.run_in_executor(ThreadPoolExecutor, ...). A blocked loop causes 'heartbeat blocked for more than 10 seconds' warnings and gateway disconnects. (2) For slash commands, always interaction.response.defer(thinking=True) within the 3-second deadline, then deliver results via the followup webhook/edit_original_response within the 15-minute token window. (3) Stream responses by accumulating tokens in a buffer and throttling message edits to ~1 edit/second (llmcord uses EDIT_DELAY_SECONDS=1) rather than editing per token, to stay under rate limits. (4) Maintain a per-channel/thread conversation context keyed off Discord reply chains (the llmcord pattern), with a bounded message cache (mutex-protected dict) to minimize redundant API fetches. (5) Run the bot's event loop on the same loop as the orchestrator if both are async; if the orchestrator owns its own loop or is sync, run the Discord client in a dedicated thread with asyncio.new_event_loop() and bridge with run_coroutine_threadsafe / loop.run_in_executor. The single-loop, fully-async approach is strongly preferred - multi-loop threading is a fallback that introduces deadlock risk (e.g. future.result() blocking the calling loop). Choose discord.py over discord-interactions/hikari for an agent harness because discord.py has the largest ecosystem, supports both prefix and slash (app) commands plus message-content intent for natural @mention chat, and gives full control of the gateway/event loop needed for tight orchestrator integration.
reference_papers: This is an engineering/integration topic with no canonical academic literature; relevant grounding comes from official protocol docs rather than papers. Authoritative references: Discord Developer Documentation - Rate Limits (per-route token buckets + global 50 req/s, 429 with retry_after header) - https://discord.com/developers/docs/topics/rate-limits ; Discord Developer Documentation - Receiving and Responding to Interactions (3-second ACK deadline, 15-minute interaction token, defer/followup model) - https://discord.com/developers/docs/interactions/receiving-and-responding ; Discord Developer Documentation - Channel Resource / Uploading Files (multipart/form-data, 25 MiB default max request size, threads) - https://discord.com/developers/docs/resources/channel . No arXiv/conference papers apply. [uncertain]
reference_repos: jakobdylanc/llmcord - the canonical ~200-line single-file discord.py LLM chatbot; reply-chain conversation context, thread branching, streamed message-edit responses (green-when-done, STREAMING_INDICATOR, EDIT_DELAY_SECONDS=1), auto message splitting over 2000 chars, mutex-protected message cache, works with any OpenAI-compatible API (Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM/OpenRouter/etc.) - https://github.com/jakobdylanc/llmcord . OoriData/Discord-AI-Agent - discord.py bot wired to LLM agents via Model Context Protocol (MCP), supports OpenAI/Anthropic/Ollama, asyncio-based, pgvector MessageDB for history, SentenceTransformer embeddings - https://github.com/OoriData/Discord-AI-Agent . braindead-dev/DARVIS - agentic Discord bot (discord.js) that dynamically generates/executes Discord API code, conversation history via reply chains, message pipeline: Message -> Filter -> Build Context -> LLM -> Execute Actions -> Respond - https://github.com/braindead-dev/DARVIS . Rapptz/discord.py - the core library; see Discussion #9498 for command-sync guidance - https://github.com/Rapptz/discord.py . kkrypt0nn/Python-Discord-Bot-Template - production-oriented discord.py template (cogs, sync handling, error handling) - https://github.com/kkrypt0nn/Python-Discord-Bot-Template .
key_libraries: discord.py (Python, >=2.4, recommended primary) - full gateway + REST wrapper with app_commands (CommandTree) for slash commands, Views/Buttons/Modals, threads, file attachments, message-content intent for @mention chat; best ecosystem and event-loop control for orchestrator integration. interactions.py / discord-py-interactions (Python, >=5.x) - interactions-focused alternative with fully automatic slash-command syncing and built-in rate-limit handling; good if the harness is slash-only. hikari + arc/lightbulb/miru (Python, hikari 2.0.0.dev*) - strongly-typed micro-framework with speedups (orjson, aiohttp[speedups], uvloop); choose for high-performance/large bots, but needs a separate command framework. Pycord (Python) - discord.py fork with convenient interaction helpers. aiohttp (Python, bundled with discord.py) - underlying async HTTP. uvloop (Python, UNIX-only) - drop-in faster event loop. litellm or openai (Python) - OpenAI-compatible client layer so one connector serves many LLM backends (llmcord uses this approach). For pure outbound notifications, the plain Discord Webhook REST endpoint (or discord-webhook / discord_notify) needs no gateway connection.
pitfalls: 1) Blocking the asyncio event loop with synchronous LLM/agent calls -> 'Shard heartbeat blocked for more than 10 seconds', gateway disconnects; fix with loop.run_in_executor or genuinely-async clients. 2) Calling tree.sync() inside on_ready - on_ready fires repeatedly on reconnect and ADDING global commands is rate-limited; instead sync via an owner-only prefix command and only when commands actually change. 3) Confusing global vs guild command sync - plain tree.sync() ignores guild commands; global propagation takes up to 1 hour, so use guild sync (or copy_global_to) for dev. 4) Editing the message on every streamed token - instantly hits rate limits; throttle edits to ~1/sec and batch tokens. 5) Typing indicator expires after ~10s for long agent runs (30-60s+) - must refresh in a background task every ~8s, and cleanly stop()/cancel it (a stuck typing indicator from missing cleanup is a common bug). 6) Silently dropping messages over 2000 chars - Discord caps at 2000 (4000 Nitro, not for bots); split at newline/paragraph boundaries with a ~1990 safety margin and never break code-block/markdown fences mid-chunk; embeds cap at 4096/description and 6000 total. 7) Missing the 3-second interaction ACK deadline - always defer() first; the token is only valid 15 minutes and is invalidated if not ACKed in 3s. 8) Assuming bots get the 25MB user/Nitro upload increase - max request size is 25 MiB and Nitro/boost increases do NOT apply to bots or normal webhooks; oversized files are rejected. 9) Hard-coding rate limits - they change; parse 429 retry_after and X-RateLimit-* headers and back off (global ~50 req/s, ~5 msgs/5s per channel). 10) future.result() deadlock - calling a blocking future result from inside the loop deadlocks streaming agents; use loop.create_task() fire-and-forget. 11) Leaking the webhook URL - it is an unauthenticated secret; anyone with it can post. 12) Notification spam burying signal - use auto-threading so a task's updates stay in one thread. 13) Not handling client disconnect / token expiry mid-stream - if the user closes Discord or the 15-minute followup window lapses while the agent is still streaming, message.edit()/followup.send() raise discord.HTTPException against a dead interaction; wrap every edit/followup in try/except and stop the stream gracefully instead of looping into errors. 14) DM vs guild context mismatch - thread-per-task isolation assumes a guild channel; channel.create_thread() fails in DMs where threads are unsupported. Detect interaction.guild is None (DM) and fall back to plain followup messages.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: Streaming LLM response via throttled message editing
  Scenario: Agent streams a long answer without hitting rate limits
    Given a user mentions the bot with a prompt
    When the agent begins generating tokens
    Then the bot sends an initial placeholder message with a streaming indicator
    And the bot edits that message at most once per second as tokens accumulate
    And when output exceeds 2000 characters the bot splits into a new message at a line boundary
    And when generation completes the bot marks the message as finished (e.g. removes the indicator / turns green)

Feature: Non-blocking slash command backed by the agent orchestrator
  Scenario: Long-running agent task respects the interaction deadline
    Given a user invokes a slash command that triggers a 40-second agent run
    When the command handler is entered
    Then the bot calls interaction.response.defer(thinking=True) within 3 seconds
    And the agent runs without blocking the event loop (offloaded via run_in_executor if synchronous)
    And a typing/working indicator is refreshed every ~8 seconds while processing
    And the final result is delivered via the followup webhook within the 15-minute token window

Feature: Rate-limit-safe delivery
  Scenario: Bot receives HTTP 429 while editing a message
    Given the bot is editing a streamed response
    When Discord returns a 429 Too Many Requests with a retry_after value
    Then the bot waits for retry_after seconds before retrying
    And the bot does not crash or drop the in-progress message
    And the bot honors the global ~50 requests/second and per-channel limits

Feature: Per-task session isolation via threads
  Scenario: Two concurrent slash commands do not cross-contaminate output
    Given two /task commands are submitted concurrently in the same channel
    When both tasks begin streaming
    Then each task creates and streams into its own dedicated thread
    And neither task's streamed tokens appear in the other task's thread
    And when the interaction occurs in a DM (interaction.guild is None) the connector falls back to plain followup messages instead of creating a thread
optimal_implementation: Provide an async DiscordConnector class on the orchestrator's event loop. Sketch: class DiscordConnector with __init__(token, orchestrator, edit_interval=1.0) building commands.Bot with intents.message_content=True. Register a slash command 'ask' whose handler does interaction.response.defer(thinking=True) (beats the 3s deadline) then calls _stream(interaction.followup, channel, prompt). Register on_message: ignore bot authors, require bot in msg.mentions, wrap work in 'async with msg.channel.typing()' and call _stream. _stream(sink, channel, prompt): keep buf='', sent=None, last=0.0; 'async for token in self._agen(prompt)': append to buf, and only when (loop.time()-last)>=edit_interval call _emit and update last; finally _emit(final=True). _agen: if orchestrator is an async generator just 'async for t in orchestrator.stream(prompt): yield t'; if synchronous, offload via 'await loop.run_in_executor(None, lambda: list(orchestrator.run(prompt)))' and yield chunks. _emit(sink, sent, text, final=False): clamp text to 1990 chars (+ a streaming indicator unless final); retry loop up to 5x: if sent is None await sink.send(text) else await sent.edit(content=text); on discord.HTTPException with status==429 await asyncio.sleep(e.retry_after) and retry, else raise. start(): await self.bot.start(token). Sync commands once via an owner-only prefix command (NOT on_ready); use guild sync in dev. For outbound agent notifications with no interactivity, skip the gateway and POST to a Webhook URL via discord.Webhook.from_url(...).send(embed=...), auto-threading per task. For >2000 chars split on newline boundaries keeping code fences intact; for files use channel.send(file=discord.File(...)) respecting the 25 MiB request cap. Run with asyncio.run(connector.start()); enable uvloop on UNIX for throughput.
sota_improvements: Beyond a basic send-after-completion bot: (1) Adopt llmcord's reply-chain conversation model - derive context from Discord's native reply graph and thread structure instead of a custom session store, with a bounded mutex-protected message cache. (2) Throttled edit-streaming (EDIT_DELAY ~1s) plus a finished-state marker for live UX without rate-limit bans. (3) A refreshing typing/working indicator (every ~8s) with guaranteed cancellation in finally to avoid stuck indicators. (4) Hybrid transport: gateway Bot for interactive flows + fire-and-forget Webhooks for agent notifications, auto-threading each task so updates stay grouped. (5) MCP-based tool integration (as in OoriData/Discord-AI-Agent) so the connector exposes Discord actions to the agent as tools rather than hard-coding them. (6) Backend-agnostic LLM layer via an OpenAI-compatible client (litellm) so one connector serves many models, with a /model slash command for runtime switching. (7) Hot-reloadable config and per-user/role/channel allow/block lists for access control. (8) Robust 429 handling that parses retry_after and X-RateLimit headers with exponential backoff instead of hard-coded sleeps. (9) Performance: aiohttp[speedups] + orjson + uvloop. (10) Graceful long-output handling: code-block-aware splitting and offering an attachment/paste-link fallback when output is very large.
